description: Generic example deny-list. Each pattern is a JavaScript regular expression source. A write that matches a block entry in any string field (including object keys, decoded segments and the joined fields of one write) is rejected. A review entry holds the write for a person instead. An optional validate check must also pass for a match to count. Patterns must stay fast on long input: the gate times each one at startup and refuses slow ones. Replace or extend this list for your own data; the server refuses to start if the list is missing, empty, invalid or slow.

patterns.description: Email addresses. The local part is anchored to the start of its run and bounded, so matching stays linear on long tokens.
An email address written with the at sign or dot spelled out, e.g. name [at] host [dot] com. Held for review: ordinary prose can look similar.

US-style phone numbers written with separators or a parenthesized area code, e.g. 555-010-0199, (555)010-0199 or +1 555 010 0199. Toll-free numbers (800, 833, 844, 855, 866, 877, 888) are public organization lines and do not count.
Numbers in the 3-2-4 social security number format, separated by hyphens or spaces
A birth-date label or the word born, followed by a full date (01/02/1980, 1980-01-02, January 2 1980 or 2 January 1980)
A record-number label (MRN, M.R.N., MR#, medical record number, patient ID, chart number) followed by an identifier with four or more digits, optionally with a short letter prefix or digit groups
Card numbers of 13 to 19 digits, optionally grouped, that pass the Luhn checksum
Medicare Beneficiary Identifier format (11 characters, letters exclude S, L, O, I, B and Z), with or without hyphens
IPv4 addresses. Held for review rather than blocked, because four-part version numbers look the same.
A house number, one to three capitalized words and a street suffix. Held for review: this is a heuristic, not an address parser.
A capitalized name after a patient, member or honorific cue, e.g. Patient Jane Synthetic or Mrs. Synthetic. Held for review: this is a heuristic, not name recognition.
